text:
[LNUL.4.10] **A `null` operand does not absorb a fault.** For every operator other than
`and` / `or` ([LNUL.4.2]) and `??` ([LNUL.8.9]), and for the arguments of every builtin
call, the engine must yield the result of evaluating every operand. If an operand faults,
as [LNUL.4.2] defines it, the expression yields a fault whatever the other operands are,
`null` included; [LNUL.4.1]'s propagation applies only when no operand faults.

When several operands fault, the expression yields one, chosen by [LNUL.4.2]'s order. An
operand's position never enters, so `a + b` and `b + a` yield the same fault on every
input. Only that fault reaches a surface ([LERR.1.4.11]). The engine may evaluate the
operands in any order.

A `null` operand still prevents the operation itself ([LNUL.9.3]), and a fault comes only
from evaluating an operand or from performing the operation. So `x / z` with `x` null and
`z` zero is `null`: the division is not performed, and there is no zero divisor to refuse.

idris.name: lnul_4_10__cast_of_a_trap_is_the_trap
idris.note: The cast: an operand that faults is the fault, for either form and every target.

idris.name: lnul_4_10__null_beside_a_trap_is_the_trap
idris.note: A trap on either side of a binary operator is the expression's answer whatever the other operand is, null included, for every operator over values. The choice between two faults by [LNUL.4.2]'s kind order, and the arguments of a builtin call, are not modelled: the evaluator has one trap.

idris.name: lnul_4_10__tag_test_of_a_trap_is_the_trap
idris.note: The unary case: an operand of `is` or `is not` that faults is the expression's answer, for every subject and either polarity.

idris.name: lnul_9_3__null_before_the_divisor
idris.note: The last paragraph: a null operand prevents the operation, so null / 0, null // 0 and null % 0 are null and no zero divisor is refused, on either side and for every arithmetic operator of the fragment -- the clause's own example, `/`, included.
